_note: TEACHES THE DRAGON CLAIM (PLAN.md 13.2). Won by killing the mother AND holding the
nest until the hatchling grows.
⚠️ IT USED TO BE `last_man_standing`, AND THAT WAS A DIFFERENT MISSION FROM THE ONE ITS
OWN BRIEFING DESCRIBED. The file said 'Destroy The Dragon AND Tame the baby' and then
declared conquest, so the actual win was 'leave the passive opponent nothing' -- a
player could finish this scenario without ever crossing the river, and a player who did
everything the briefing asked would still be sitting there afterwards. PLAN.md 15.8
logged it as 'scenario 4's briefing promises a dragon its map has not got' and parked
the fix at 16.10; 13.2b made the whole rule real on 2026-09-06, so it is fixed here
instead.
TWO WIN ROWS, ANDed, which is what multiple `win` rows mean (PLAN.md 11.8) and the
shape scenario 1 already uses. THE SECOND IMPLIES THE FIRST -- you cannot own a dragon
without having killed her -- and the first is written anyway, because it is the half of
the goal the player can finish in the first few minutes. Without it the tracker shows
one unticked line for six minutes after the fight is won, which reads as 'nothing I did
counted'.
⚠️ `owner: "gaia"` IS WHY THIS SCENARIO NEEDED A LINE OF CODE AT ALL. The mother is a
UNIQUE unit and the obvious spelling is `subject: "named_unit"` -- which is refused
until 16.7's per-entity overrides exist, and rightly so. What she actually is, to
anything that can count today, is `unit.dragon` belonging to owner 0; and `owner` had
no way to say owner 0, because a player number below 1 is refused (it is a typo
everywhere else). So `ObjectiveDef.Owner` gained `GAIA`, appended for the wire's sake,
and `ObjectiveSystem._owners_for` answers it with the literal [0] rather than through
`Diplomacy` -- see that file's trap 1, which this deliberately does not weaken.
⚠️ THE ONE WAY THIS SCENARIO CAN DEAD-END, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS UNREACHABLE RATHER
THAN IMPOSSIBLE: if the mother dies to something that is not a player, row 1 ticks and
row 2 never can. `NestSystem._start_claims` requires `last_attacker_owner > 0`, so a
mother killed by gaia or by a debug destroy hatches nothing, and `claim_owner` is never
cleared -- there is no second chance at her. In play there is no route to it: wildlife
does not attack gaia (`Diplomacy`), and the only other killers are a falling building
and `DebugDestroyCommand`. Left unguarded on purpose. A guard would mean either
re-opening a spent claim or reviving her, and both are new rules for a case a real
player cannot reach.
STARTS IN AGE 4, THE AGE OF DRAGONS, and that is not flavour: the army below is
castle-tier and the mission is a fight, not an economy. Scenario 2 is the age ladder's
lesson and this one must not repeat it -- six minutes of holding ground is long enough
without 500 food first.
THE ARMY AND THE NEST ARE BOTH IN `map.json`, NOT IN THIS FILE. A saved map is the
per-scenario starting-entity list, and `MapGen.build_from` spawns exactly what it
lists. `dev_preview/preview_author_maps.gd` is what stamped them -- the nest and the
mother from `MapGenerator` itself (13.2a places one of each on every generated map),
the 25 units from that file's `GARRISONS` table. To change either, edit there and
re-run it with `--force --campaign HowToPlay --scenario scenario_4`. A `starting_units`
field HERE would be a number that does nothing until somebody remembered to re-author
the map, which is the seed trap wearing a different hat.
⚠️ THE NUMBER IN `message` IS THE NUMBER IN THAT TABLE and a test asserts the briefing
still names it. It moved TWICE in one day, both times off a real play-through: 155
units, then 75, then 25. The prose is exactly the kind of thing a data edit leaves
behind, and a briefing promising an army three times the size of the one on the map is
the same defect this scenario was rewritten to fix, at a smaller size.
THE FIRST DRAFT WAS WRONG BY A FACTOR OF SIX AND NO TEST COULD HAVE SAID SO. 155 was
arrived at by asking what 'an army' looks like; 25 is what killing one dragon actually
takes. An authored fight's difficulty is a property of the FIGHT -- the same shape as
PLAN.md 11.8's note that an authored target's reachability is a property of the MAP and
not of the roster.
⚠️ THE PLAYER OPENS AT 31/10 POPULATION and can train nothing until the army thins
out. That is `PopulationSystem`'s declared direction (report the truth, refuse only the
next order) and it is not a dead end -- losses free the cap. The answer to it has twice
been to cut the ARMY rather than raise the cap: covering it means houses or a castle,
and a castle trains and shoots, which would change the mission.
THE OPPONENT IS STILL PASSIVE and is now almost scenery: it runs its economy, never
attacks, and cannot be the reason this is won or lost. Elimination is still the loss,
as it is on every map in this game, which is why no lose row is written.
name: How To Find a Dragon and Tame It
description: A dragon guards her nest down by the river, midway between the two towns. Kill her, then hold the nest while her hatchling grows -- six minutes, and it is yours.
message:
Objective: Kill the mother dragon, then hold her nest until the hatchling grows.

Overview: You start in the Age of Dragons with 25 elite swordsmen already at your town centre. Drag a box around them to select them, then use the minimap to find the standing stones by the river, near the middle of the map.

The mother flies and hits hard. Send all of them.

When she dies a hatchling appears at the nest, and SIX MINUTES later it becomes your dragon. It is not yours until then: if the nest is destroyed, or the hatchling is killed, the claim is lost for good. Keep your army on the nest until the dragon takes wing.
_note_map: THE MAP IS THE SAVED map.png BESIDE THIS FILE (2.4c, PLAN.md 11.3). `seed` is
PROVENANCE ONLY -- build_config() never calls MapGenerator, so a generator change
cannot move the nest this scenario is authored around.
⚠️ THE BRIEFING NO LONGER SAYS 'ACROSS THE RIVER', AND THAT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN
REWORDED FOR STYLE. `_place_nest` put the nest at (55, 55) with the starts at (65, 30)
and (30, 65), and this map's river is a broken diagonal band with dry gaps -- so the
line from player 1's start to the nest is 25 tiles of unbroken grass and crosses no
water at all. Sampled off map.png's R channel, which is the only channel that is data.
'Across the river' is how this file described a dragon it did not have; writing it
again about a dragon on the player's own bank would be the same defect at a smaller
size. The nest is on player 1's side, which is asymmetric and costs nothing here: the
opponent is Passive and is never going to contest it.
THE SEED IS UNCHANGED AND THE TERRAIN CAME BACK IDENTICAL -- same size, same two
starts. What changed is five trees (the nest clears its own ground, `_claim_her_reach`)
plus the nest, the mother and the garrison. That is `_place_nest`'s documented claim
about not disturbing the RNG stream, confirmed on a real map.

objectives.subject: unit
objectives.text: Hold the nest and claim her hatchling
